text:
Morgan: morning — seeing apiserver slow startup in eu-west-2 after the 02:00 rollout. lots of watch reconnects, leader flipped twice. several pods in gpu-pool stuck Pending.
Andy: which rollout? controller-manager or infra?
Morgan: looks like a tiny controller-manager PID bump, but the timing matches a big node attach wave. logs show lots of tcp resets and dns failures.
Morgan: logs snippet:
```
E0301 02:03:12.123 apiserver watch: error response 500
rpc: read tcp 10.2.3.4:6443: i/o timeout
I0301 02:03:13.789 leaderElection: lost lock, trying to renew
```
Priya: Cloud metrics show nat/conntrack spiking — conntrack table approaching full then SNAT failures. kube-proxy flips when that happens. likely cause: GPU node attach storm.
Jin: we kicked ~45 GPU nodes online at ~01:55 for a capacity run. autoscaler did parallel attaches (default batch). saw device attach churn + iptables reloads on the nodes.
sre-bot: :rotating_light: alert: apiserver.watch.latency > 5s in eu-west-2 (triggered 02:03)
Morgan: can someone tail kube-proxy logs on the affected nodes? look for conntrack/table-full or iptables-restore errors.
Andy: on it — tailing kube-proxy on node euw2-gpu-17: `iptables-restore: line 342: error` and `nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet`
Priya: that matches. conntrack full => SNAT fails => upstream clients get RST => controller-manager can't renew leases -> leader election jitter and apiserver watch churn.
Jin: quick mitigation: reduce attach concurrency (throttle onboarding). I'll pause the autoscaler and set parallel attaches to 5/s. also can restart kube-proxy on hot nodes to free conntrack and reload rules.
Morgan: rollback controller-manager patch?
Priya: rollback won't fix conntrack pressure. need to relieve NAT first. rollback might be unnecessary and could disrupt other fixes.
Andy: restarted kube-proxy on 5 nodes with highest `nf_conntrack_count`. seeing immediate drop in conntrack usage and fewer iptables errors.
Morgan: apiserver watch latency trending back to normal, leader stabilized. nice work. :thumbsup:
Jin: filed INFRA ticket INFRA-2026: "gpu-onboard-attach-throttle-and-conntrack-safeguards" — includes actions: autoscaler backpressure on conntrack, synthetic watcher alert, bump default conntrack table for gpu nodepool, and add pre-onboard drain of conntrack slack.
Priya: follow-ups: add a metric to the autoscaler for `node.nf_conntrack_used_pct` and circuit-break onboarding when >70%. add a runbook entry for kube-proxy restarts during attach storms.
Morgan: closing notes: incident mitigated, but we should also audit any other clusters where large onboarding coincides with apiserver leader instability.
sre-bot: incident resolved (1715554321) — mitigated at 02:11.
Andy: :eyes: will put a short postmortem on the ticket and link relevant logs.
